get.description: The delistings of a currency, newest first, at most 100, with their steps and when each was applied.
get.summary: List the delistings of a currency

default.description: Any other error, in the envelope with a code

post.description: Schedules the steps that take an approved currency to delisted. A delisting that stopped before delisted, such as an emergency halt, stays scheduled, so that it can be cancelled to relist the currency; a new delisting supersedes it and takes the currency on from its state, with steps after it. A standard delisting starts with delist_announced; an emergency one, for a security or regulatory reason, at trading_halted or later. The steps follow the order of the lifecycle (delist_announced, deposits_disabled, sell_only, trading_halted, withdrawal_only, frozen, delisted), each at a later time, and any of them may be left out. Each step is applied at its time by the scheduler of the instances, exactly once, and changes the capabilities of the currency; a step that is due is applied at once. The settlement says what happens at frozen to the balances that are left: convert into another approved currency at a price, or hold for a claim; it is recorded and announced now, and carried out by the ledger. Audited as currency.delisting_schedule, and each step as currency.lifecycle_change.
post.summary: Schedule the delisting of a currency

default.description: Any other error, in the envelope with a code

post.description: Cancels a scheduled delisting before it reaches frozen: its steps that are left are not applied, and the currency returns to active with every capability of that state. At frozen and after, balances are settled, and a cancel answers 409 delisting_irreversible. With version, a cancel based on another version of the delisting answers 409 version_conflict. Audited as currency.delisting_cancel.
post.summary: Cancel the delisting of a currency

default.description: Any other error, in the envelope with a code

get.description: The migrations that the currency is the target or a source of, newest first, at most 100, with their sources, phases, and when each applied.
get.summary: List the migrations of a currency

default.description: Any other error, in the envelope with a code

post.description: Schedules a rebrand, a redenomination, or a merger that moves the holders of one or more approved source currencies to this approved target, each source at its ratio: the units of the target that one unit of the source becomes, such as 0.01 for 100 LEND = 1 AAVE. The phases follow the order announced, deposits_paused, trading_halted, converting, completed; announced and completed are required. A forced migration pauses the deposits and withdrawals of its sources at deposits_paused, halts their trading and conversions at trading_halted, and retires them from the lists at completed; an optional one only offers the conversion, and its sources stay. Each phase applies at its time, exactly once, on any instance. From announced on, the sources show the migration. Conversions round down to the precision of the target and record the dust; they are carried out by the ledger. Audited as currency.migration_schedule, and each phase as currency.migration_phase.
post.summary: Schedule a migration into a currency

default.description: Any other error, in the envelope with a code

post.description: Cancels a migration into this currency before it converts: the phases that are left do not apply, and its sources get back what its phases paused. From converting on, a cancel answers 409 migration_irreversible. With version, a cancel based on another version answers 409 version_conflict. Audited as currency.migration_cancel.

default.description: Any other error, in the envelope with a code

post.description: Undoes a delete: the currency keeps its hk, symbol, and contract, and comes back as pending, so that it is public again only once an administrator approves it. With version, the restore is refused with 409 version_conflict when the currency has changed since. A currency that is not deleted answers 409 not_deleted.

parameters.description: The version the restore is based on
parameters.name: version

default.description: Any other error, in the envelope with a code

delete.description: A rebrand keeps the symbol before as a previous symbol of the currency: the lists find the currency by it, and no other currency can take it, which answers 409 symbol_reserved. Releasing it lets another currency take it, and the currency is no longer found by it. The current symbol cannot be released. Audited as currency.symbol_release.
delete.summary: Release a previous symbol of a currency

post.description: After a review found the current values of a row that did not match its seal right, as after a reviewed data fix, seals the row again with the current row-mac key and closes the finding. It needs two administrators: the first request records the reason and answers 202 with the finding and who asked; the same request by another administrator within 24 hours re-seals the row and answers 200. The administrator who asked cannot approve (403 second_approval_required), and neither step is open to the administrator whose account the row belongs to (403 own_row). The reason is required. Audited as integrity.reseal_request and integrity.reseal, with the values sealed now, secret ones masked. A finding that is already resolved answers 409 already_resolved; without data keys, 503. The route needs a step-up.

Administrators are never closed out, and the sessions of users are kept. The control applies from starts_at (now when absent) until it is lifted or reaches ends_at, on every instance within platform.poll_interval_ms. Users see it on the status endpoint and over the WebSocket from announce_at. Audited as platform.control_create.

An active lockdown of a feature in platform.lift_approval (withdrawals and trading by default) needs two administrators: the first call records the request and answers 202, and a call by another administrator lifts it; the same administrator gets 409 second_approval_required. With version, the lift is refused with 409 version_conflict when the control has changed since. An ended or lifted control answers 409 control_ended. Audited as platform.control_lift_request and platform.control_lift.

The restriction applies until it is lifted or reaches ends_at. The reason, case, and note are never shown to the user. A wrong recovery code answers 401 recovery_code_invalid, leaves the challenge usable, and counts toward the lock of the password: 429 password_locked with Retry-After.
